source_text: Quoquo modo sit erratum, tam diu utique regnavit error quam diu haereses non erant. Aliquos Marcionitas et Valentinianos liberanda veritas expectabat. Interea perperam evangelizabatur, perperam credebatur; tot milia milium perperam tincta, tot opera fidei perperam administrate, tot virtutes, tot charismata perperam operata, tot sacerdotia, tot ministeria perperam functa, tot denique martyria perperam coronata. Aut si non perperam nec in vacuum quale est, ut ante res dei currerent quam cuius dei notum esset? ante Christiani quam Christus inventus? ante haereses quam vera doctrina? Sed enim in omnibus veritas imaginem antecedit, post vero similitudo succedit. Ceterum satis ineptum, ut pro priori doctrina haeresis habeatur, vel quoniam ipsa est quae futuras haereses cavendas praenuntiabat. Ad eius doctrinae ecclesiam scriptum est, immo ipsa doctrina ad ecclesiam scribit, Et si angelus de caelo aliter evangelizaverit, citra quam nos, anathema sit.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that if the apostolic doctrine had been wrong, error would have reigned unchecked until the heretics appeared, which is absurd.
pass_a_gloss: In whatever way the error happened, at any rate error reigned as long as heresies did not exist. The truth that was to be set free was waiting for some Marcionites and Valentinians. Meanwhile the gospel was preached wrongly, belief was wrong; so many thousands of thousands were wrongly baptized, so many works of faith were wrongly performed, so many powers, so many gifts of grace were wrongly worked, so many priesthoods, so many ministries were wrongly discharged, so many martyrdoms were wrongly crowned. Or if not wrongly and not in vain, what sort of thing is it, that the things of God ran their course before it was known of what God they were? that people were Christians before Christ was found? that heresies existed before true doctrine? But in all things truth precedes the image, and afterwards the likeness follows. For the rest, it is quite absurd that heresy should be held as the earlier doctrine, especially since it is that very doctrine which foretold that future heresies must be guarded against. To the church of that doctrine it was written, rather that doctrine itself writes to the church, 'Even if an angel from heaven should preach the gospel differently than we do, let him be anathema.'

choices.why: The adverb is repeated five times for rhetorical force; 'wrongly' preserves the blunt, repetitive condemnation without softening it.
The literal sense is 'dipped,' but in Christian Latin this is the standard term for baptism; the glossary context requires the Christian technical sense.
The Greek loanword refers to spiritual gifts; rendering it as 'gifts of grace' keeps the technical Pauline sense clear for a first-time reader.
The Greek loanword is kept as 'anathema' because it is a technical term of condemnation; translating it as 'accursed' would lose the formulaic force.
In Tertullian's argument, truth precedes its image or copy; 'image' preserves the Platonic contrast between original and likeness.
Paired with 'image,' this word completes the contrast between original truth and derivative copy; 'likeness' keeps the parallel.

bible_refs.note: Et si angelus de caelo aliter evangelizaverit, citra quam nos, anathema sit

pass_b_english: However the error came about, error certainly reigned as long as there were no heresies. Truth was waiting to set free some Marcionites and Valentinians. In the meantime the gospel was preached wrongly, faith was believed wrongly; so many thousands upon thousands were wrongly baptized, so many works of faith were wrongly performed, so many miracles, so many gifts of grace were wrongly worked, so many priesthoods, so many ministries were wrongly fulfilled, so many martyrdoms were wrongly crowned. Or if not wrongly and not in vain, what kind of thing is it that the things of God ran ahead before it was known whose God they were? Christians before Christ was found? Heresies before true doctrine? But in all things truth precedes the image; the likeness follows after. Otherwise it is quite absurd that heresy should be taken for the earlier doctrine, especially since it is the true doctrine itself that foretold that future heresies must be guarded against. It was written to the church of that doctrine—indeed, the doctrine itself writes to the church: "Even if an angel from heaven should preach a gospel other than the one we preached to you, let him be anathema" (Galatians 1:8).

problems.quote: Truth was waiting for some Marcionites and Valentinians to set her free.
problems.source_quote: Aliquos Marcionitas et Valentinianos liberanda veritas expectabat.
problems.why: Latin says truth expects to free them; English reverses who is acting.
problems.fix: Truth expected to set free some Marcionites and Valentinians.

edits.old: Truth was waiting for some Marcionites and Valentinians to set her free.
edits.new: Truth was waiting to set free some Marcionites and Valentinians.

fixed: Agency: 'liberanda veritas expectabat' means truth was waiting to set them free, not waiting for them to set her free.

last_rejected.quote: what kind of thing is it that the things of God ran ahead before it was known whose God they were?
last_rejected.source_quote: quale est, ut ante res dei currerent quam cuius dei notum esset?
last_rejected.why: 'cuius dei' means 'which God's', i.e. which God they belonged to, not 'whose God they were'.
last_rejected.fix: what kind of thing is it that the things of God ran ahead before it was known which God's they were?
last_rejected.ruling: English 'whose God they were' conveys 'cuius dei' meaning 'of which God', preserving sense.

last_rejected.quote: so many miracles, so many gifts of grace were wrongly worked
last_rejected.source_quote: tot virtutes, tot charismata perperam operata
last_rejected.why: "virtutes" means virtues, not miracles; the English omits virtues and adds miracles.
last_rejected.fix: so many virtues, so many gifts of grace were wrongly worked
last_rejected.ruling: In early Christian Latin, 'virtutes' commonly means miraculous powers; 'miracles' is within normal range, not a major error.
